patches.reason: Shell bootstrap (issue #3). (1) Removes the assembly of location.origin into a ServerConnection: in this Android WebView shell the asset origin http://127.0.0.1:18090 is a static asset server, not an OpenCode service, so that connection could only fail its health check. The ?auth_token URL passthrough is inapplicable for the same reason (no assembled server to authenticate) and is removed with its cleanup helper. (2) Bootstraps the first-party host registry via createMobileHosts (fail-closed host-key stub + Null credential resolver; real counterparts are issues #6/#4) and injects hosts.upstreamConnections() - a solid-store-derived reactive value - as the app's servers prop; direct servers are added through the app's own dialog into the upstream persisted list. Not implemented via the VITE_OPENCODE_SERVER_MODE=none build-time variable on purpose: that would hide the behavior behind build configuration and complicate rebasing; this patch keeps the change visible and rebaseable in one place. M-007 amendment (issue #4): the entry now also creates the device credential vault client (createVaultClient over createWebMessageChannelTransport) with the handshake listener registered before first render - shape-validated only (event.origin is never consulted: embedder-posted messages carry an empty origin by platform construction), port captured inside the transport closure, acked immediately, later handshakes ignored - and passes the vault plus a vault-backed resolver into createMobileHosts. Before the ack the vault is unavailable (explicit state, no plaintext fallback).

patches.reason: Optional 'remember credential' for the connect dialog's password method (issue #4). The checkbox participates only when rendered AND the shell vault is available; the decision itself (truth table v3, 12 rows) lives in the first-party package (packages/mobile-hosts src/vault/remember.ts) so it is unit-tested and probe-able, and this patch only translates it into vault put/remove calls and the constructed connection. Rows 2/12 abort the save with an inline needs-password message (never cast an empty value); the early-exit is forced off when the checkbox state differs from the prior's remembered flag; a failed put/remove keeps the dialog open with an inline error. Vault unavailable renders the checkbox disabled plus an explicit-state note - no plaintext fallback anywhere.

patches.reason: Hydration credential resolution (issue #4). After the persisted server list hydrates, stored http entries that carry a credential reference but no password get the password resolved from the shell vault and injected into the in-memory solid store ONLY - the M-002 encode path runs on every persist write, so the value can never reach a persistent backend; it merely spares re-typing within the session. Vault-level unavailability and per-entry corrupt/unsupported resolve to nothing and the server's own authentication flow takes over (docs/design/units/connection.md failure matrix; no plaintext fallback).

patches.reason: Platform fetch injection with the validated-follow policy (issue #5, decision 0002 D1). createSecureFetch from the first-party package keeps redirect:"follow" (legitimate same-origin reverse proxies keep working) and validates the FINAL response before body delivery: a cross-host final URL is refused with the body cancelled, an https-to-http downgrade is refused, and a request URL carrying userinfo credentials is refused before anything is sent. Coverage: platform.fetch feeds createServerTransport (API/SSE/binary reads) and the health checks; the upload XHR is validated separately by M-012 with the same rules, and the pairing-flow residual fetch surface (OpenCode.make + checkServerHealth(globalThis.fetch) in pairing.ts) is registered out-of-scope in docs/design/units/connection.md. Auth-header semantics are untouched (the Basic header is built upstream exactly as before); cross-origin redirect sub-requests already lose the Authorization header by browser spec, so the wrapper is the shell's own fail-closed layer, not a leak fix. The embedded marker 'mobile(M-011): platform fetch validated-follow (origin + downgrade checked before body delivery)' survives minification and anchors V-conn dist verification.

patches.reason: Validated-follow for the upload face (issue #5, decision 0002 D1). The attachment upload is the one request that bypasses the platform fetch seam (M-011) - it goes through XMLHttpRequest for progress and streaming - so the same URL policy from the first-party package is enforced here: userinfo credential URLs are refused before anything is sent (D-URL), and on load the FINAL xhr.responseURL must still be same-origin with the request and must not have downgraded https-to-http, else the body is rejected (SecureFetchError) instead of being read as the server's upload receipt. Cross-origin redirect sub-requests already lose the Authorization header by browser spec (the floor); this patch is the shell's own fail-closed layer on top.

patches.reason: Probe-classified connect errors on the save path (issue #5, decision 0002 D4). The endpoint probe is dispatched BEFORE the authoritative health check (so its classification is usually already resolved when the verdict arrives) but only chooses the error WORDING after the check failed - the health check stays the sole authority for whether a save proceeds, and a probe verdict can never pass a save it refused. Error-message precedence: the upstream mixed-content structural signal, then the check's own unauthorized flag (authoritative 401), then the probe's transport classification (dialog.server.error.<code>), then the generic upstream message as the EXPLICIT degrade when the probe is unavailable, answered ok, or conflicts with the real fetch - a classification is never fabricated. A userinfo credential URL is refused up front with the precise credential-url message (D-URL). App-i18n keys only (en base merged with the locale table; missing key falls back to en, then to the key itself) - the first-party mobile-hosts direct.error.* keys are a separate set for first-party UI surfaces (F5).

patches.reason: Probe bridge wiring (issue #5). The entry creates the endpoint probe client over the protocol-isolated probe transport (independent opencode-mobile-probe-handshake string, shape-validated capture with exactly one port, port confined to the transport closure, acked immediately, later handshakes ignored, event.origin never consulted - embedder-posted messages carry an empty origin by platform construction) and passes it into createMobileHosts alongside the vault. The two bridges sit on the same window message events but each captures only its own handshake string, so neither can capture the other's port and the vault gates C1-C5 are not perturbed. Before the native ack the probe stays unavailable (fail-closed); a never-acked bridge degrades the dialog to the generic error message.

patches.reason: SSH tunnel bridge wiring (issue #6). The entry creates the ssh transport synchronously during module evaluation, before asynchronous locale loading, so its window-message listener cannot miss native startup. It signals readiness through an AndroidX WebMessageListener bootstrap; native restricts that bootstrap to the exact configured loopback origin and main frame before posting the existing protocol-isolated channel (`opencode-mobile-ssh-handshake`). The transferred port stays closure-confined, is ack-gated, and retains the existing JSON/requestId operation API. createMobileHosts receives the bridge-backed hostKey verifier, tunnel transport and sshBridge handle; fail-closed stubs remain the package's no-injection default.

Real SSH/host-key confirmation remains unverified.

patches.reason: Service ops bridge wiring (issue #7). The entry creates the fourth protocol-isolated sibling transport over the svcops handshake (opencode-mobile-svcops-handshake) and registers the bridge-backed client through the module-level service ops seam (setActiveServiceOpsPort) - the createMobileHosts option contract stays unchanged (plan zero-change list: runtime.ts untouched). Before the native ack the service ops panel stays degraded-hidden (fail-closed stub): a client-only build implies no service-operation surface. The bridge protocol carries {templateId, params, os} ONLY, never a command string - the command face is the native-side whitelist (ServiceCommandValidator) assembled behind the single gated setCommand call site; the credential is resolved per command by the panel and crosses one way, exactly once, never logged or echoed (N7).

patches.reason: Wires the Home session row archive action to the real API (issue #8). The generated client has exposed session.update with an archived flag all along (PATCH /api/session/:id, body archived; the server stamps time.archived); the upstream UI kept a stub that always rejected ('Session archiving is unavailable' next to a TODO). The stub becomes a real call and the success path drops the row from the 'home-sessions' query cache and invalidates/re-syncs the canonical session record (so the locally known copy carries the archived stamp and is filtered by the home index merge, home/sessions/index.ts parseHomeSessionIndex); the tabs cleanup and the onError toast are the existing archiveHomeSession helper semantics (archive.test.ts), which this patch does not touch. Archiving is a reversible metadata operation, not a deletion: no danger confirmation (the zero-delete red line does not apply), and there is still no unarchive UI - the same gap exists upstream and is recorded as an accepted limitation in docs/design/units/projects-sessions.md.

patches.reason: Files bridge wiring + platform file capabilities (issue #16). The entry creates the FIFTH protocol-isolated sibling transport over the files handshake (opencode-mobile-files-handshake) and registers the bridge-backed client through the module-level files seam (setActiveFilesPort) - the createMobileHosts option contract stays unchanged (the M-016 registration shape). web.ts completes the two Platform fields that were desktop-only declarations on web: readClipboardImage (comment anchor 'Read image from clipboard (desktop only)' - the desktop implementation is not in this closure) and saveFile (session export + GUI-extension system.save routes). Both read the port through the seam PER CALL; before the bridge acks the fail-closed stub answers (clipboardImage null / saveFile false / shareDataUrl false). Platform TYPES are untouched - both fields are pre-existing optional members, so the diff carries zero type-level change. The saveFile stub false vs the absent-field anchor fallback is an intentional behavior change (silent cancel instead of a fake-success toast for a download that is a dead point inside the WebView shell), registered in docs/design/units/attachments-artifacts.md and gated by G27 item 8.

patches.reason: Timeline attachment share face (issue #16). openAttachment's data: branch - the only branch where the DEVICE holds the bytes (the base64 rides the message part) - prefers the bridge share before the anchor download; the passed name is the SAME source as the anchor.download (getFilename(file.name) || 'attachment') and is sanitized again inside the first-party client (JS sanitizeFilename + Kotlin FILENAME native re-check). Success resolves true (done); cancel (false), a throw, or a bridge-less environment all fall back to the upstream anchor.download verbatim - behavior is never worse than upstream (plan L6 fixed reading: false falls back). The file:// URI branch is REMOTELY-held identity: its bytes never entered the device (schema.ts PathAttachmentPart anchor 'its bytes never enter the draft store'), so the branch is byte-for-byte untouched - no device-side share or path resolution for remote artifacts.

patches.reason: Notifications bridge wiring (issue #23). The entry creates the SIXTH protocol-isolated sibling transport over the notifications handshake (opencode-mobile-notifications-handshake) and registers the bridge-backed client through the module-level notifications seam (setActiveNotificationsPort) - the createMobileHosts option contract stays unchanged (the M-016/M-020 registration shape). Before the native ack the notifications port stays a fail-closed stub: notify answers {posted:false, code:'unavailable'} - the exact pre-issue state, because the Web Notification API behind platform.notify is a structural dead point in the Android WebView. The bridge is notification-ONLY (op whitelist {notify, requestPermission}, no reply/cancel/interrupt face), so a notification can never approve a permission or stop a task.

patches.reason: Notification delivery reroute + the permission notification face (issue #23). (1) The two system-notification call faces in handleSessionIdle/handleSessionError move from platform.notify (whose Web Notification API implementation is a structural dead point in the Android WebView; its title/description/onClick signature also cannot carry the category and tap route) to activeNotificationsPort().notify({category, title, body, route: sessionHref(input.key, sessionID)}) - the coordinator.system wrapper is UNCHANGED (event dedup + the JS front-focus suppression stay first-layer); the route is built at the only scope that knows the server key + sessionID (the onClick closure could not cross the bridge - the native side constructs the tap navigation from the route). (2) A FOURTH event listener (handlePermissionAsked) completes the upstream dead switch: the settings toggle, the sound setting and the i18n key shipped with ZERO runtime trigger in the closure; the guard chain mirrors the agent/error branches plus the auto-approve guard (project-avatar-state precedent) so a project whose requests are auto-approved NEVER notifies - the approval wire-level call sites (auto-approve + dock decide) and this face stay double-touch free. The permission payload (action/resources/message) is deliberately NOT consumed - only the session title crosses into the body; the face has no reply/cancel action (tap navigates to the session's permission dock). i18n/settings keys are all pre-existing - zero new keys in this patch.

patches.reason: Android POST_NOTIFICATIONS request face (issue #23). Turning a notification switch ON is the user-in-foreground moment: the settings face calls the bridge requestPermission op, whose NATIVE side enforces the platform conditions - API < 33 or already granted answers {granted:true} without a dialog; a request arriving without window focus answers {granted:false, code:'foreground'} and NEVER opens a dialog (the platform does not allow background permission prompts and the shell never tries).
